name: Shephatiah
overview: Shephatiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah and is notably recognized as the fifth-born son of King David. His identity is grounded in his royal lineage as one of David's sons, reflecting his place within the Davidic family. There are no additional notes or attributes recorded about him beyond his birth order and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Shephatiah means 'y-h-v-h has judged,' revealing a theologically rich meaning that acknowledges God's sovereign judgment. This proper name, recorded in 2 Samuel 3:4, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation consistent with Hebrew naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Shephatiah is explicitly identified as a son of King David and Abital, one of David's wives. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond these, emphasizing his place within the royal household as a direct descendant of David and Abital.
scriptureSignificance: Shephatiah's significance lies chiefly in his role as a son of King David, placing him within the lineage through which God's promises to David were fulfilled. Although the biblical text provides limited information about his personal deeds or influence, his inclusion among David's sons underscores the continuation of the Davidic line, which is central to the biblical narrative culminating in Christ. His name's meaning also reflects the theological theme of God's righteous judgment that permeates Scripture.
